investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official 'L'Agenda' page (following one 301 redirect the site itself issues) and one individual event detail page.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the venue's official 'L'Agenda' page (https://ducdeslombards.com/fr/l-agenda) is genuine server-rendered Drupal HTML: 39 real <article class="... mosaique-evt-item-container ..."> event cards, each stating its own title, day-name + day-number + month-abbreviation (e.g. '01 sept.'), one or more showtimes (each with its own Drupal node id via data-nid and its own time text, e.g. '19H30'), and a permalink. The page's own month/year separator headings (<div id="YYYY-MM" ... aria-label="<month> <year>">, e.g. id="2026-09" aria-label="septembre 2026") directly state, via a machine-readable id attribute, which year+month every card between one separator and the next belongs to — this fully answers the investigation question at Level 1 (a mechanical DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT combination of two retained page elements, not an escalation) with no further probing needed. A separate 'sonic-tickets-app' checkout widget is present for the booking/payment flow only, not this source's own event-discovery path. The only <script type="application/ld+json"> block on the page is a generic Article/Organization schema (no Event data).

venue_reference: Le Duc des Lombards (jazz club, rue des Lombards, Paris 1er / Les Halles)

identity.notes: The retained page's own <title> reads 'L'Agenda | Le Duc des Lombards' at the venue's own domain ducdeslombards.com, with og:site_name/twitter:site both 'Le Duc des Lombards'. The page's own footer directly states the address '42, rue des lombards / 75001 PARIS' (a Google Maps link), matching this investigation's assigned address exactly. The theme path /sites/all/themes/t_ducdeslombards/ is self-consistent with the venue's own name.

site_classification.platform: Drupal (theme path /sites/all/themes/t_ducdeslombards/) server-rendering its own event-card listing directly in HTML on the 'L'Agenda' page; a separate 'sonic-tickets-app' custom-element widget (storeUrl=https://billetterie.ducdeslombards.com) handles checkout/booking only, not event discovery.

title.notes: Each event card's own <h3 class="mosaique-evt-titre mb-xxs"> text, stated directly.

start_date.notes: Each event card's own date header states only a day name + day number + month abbreviation (e.g. '26 août') — never a year. The page's own month/year separator heading immediately preceding a card in document order (a real DOM anchor, <div id="YYYY-MM" ... aria-label="<month> <year>">, e.g. id="2026-08" aria-label="août 2026") governs every card between it and the next separator. Combining the separator's own machine-readable id ("2026-08") with the card's own day number ("26") mechanically and reproducibly yields '2026-08-26', and only that value — this project's own confirmed reading of the page's real document structure (4 separators found: 2026-08, 2026-09, 2026-10, 2026-11, each strictly preceding the cards it governs), not an assumption from today's date or typical venue habit.

derivation.rule: the nearest preceding month/year separator (a DOM element with id="YYYY-MM") governs every event card between it and the next separator in document order; concatenate the separator's own year (first 4 characters of its id) and month (next 2 characters) with the card's own day number

source_record_id.notes: Each showtime's own Drupal node id, stated directly via data-nid="(NNNNN)" — Drupal node ids are a platform-native, permanent content identifier, never reassigned to a different node once created, distinct per showtime even within one multi-night run (a run of consecutive nights, e.g. 'Du mar. 1 au jeu. 3 sept.', carries one distinct node id per night per showtime).

event_url.notes: Each card's own permalink href (/fr/l-agenda/{slug}), stated directly.

price.notes: No price/tarif text appears on the listing page's own cards. The sampled detail page's own <body> class list includes the literal class 'no-tarifs' — this Drupal template's own conditional class taxonomy directly confirming this specific record carries no price data (other events on this site may honestly carry 'has-tarifs' instead — presence genuinely varies per event within this bounded sample).
